
```{r}

rm(list=ls())
#set up environment
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(scales)
library(ggpubr)


#import list of all SNPs from VCF
snps <- read.table("/Users/erincollins/Google Drive/My Drive/Erin's Projects/chipps_gone/snp_sites_prep.txt", header = TRUE)
head(snps)
dim(snps)


#exclude loci on scaffolds because we don't know where SNPs on scaffolds fall within the genome so can't relate physical and 
#genetic distance to SNPs on chromosomes
dim(snps)
snps.chroms <- snps[which(!grepl("NW_", snps$chromosome)),]
dim(snps.chroms)
unique(snps.chroms$chromosome)



# total genome size = 2,294,859,190 bp or 2.29 Gb
#Kris Christensen et al. 2018, Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) genome and transcriptome, https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0195461&type=printable
#NCBI accession: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/assembly/GCF_018296145.1/#/st

# total genetic distance = 3119.7 cM
# McKinney et al. 2016, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1111/1755-0998.12479

# 770kb = 1cM
# O'Leary et al. 2023



#now we are going to calculate genetic distance (cM) from physical distance (bp) for each SNP
#note that we are making a very important assumption about recombination rates here: 

#       1) that the genetic distance inferred for each linkage group within the Oncorhynchus tshawytscha reference genome  (see reference above)
#          provides an accurate reflection of recombination rates for our SNPs, which are located in distinct regions
#          within each linkage group that may or may not experience the same recombination rate. 

#we are certainly violating this assumptions here, but it's the best we can do with the resources currently available for brook trout,
#or at least for the reference genome that the brook trout data are mapped to


#based on the Christensen et al 2018 PLOS ONE reference genome for Oncorhynchus tshawytscha, we know that the reference assembly is approximately 
#2.29 Gb long. We also know from this pub that the total genetic length of the linkage map is 3119.7 cM. 


#genetic distance from physical distance as follows:

#       2,294,859 kbp/3119.7 cM = 735.6 kbp/cM
#       O'Leary calculated 770 kbp/cM, which is the value used below
#       2,170,000 kbp/66.92 cM = 32,427 kbp/cM

#So, we are assuming here that every 770 kbp of physical distance on linkage group 1 is equal to 1 cM of genetic distance (big assumption).



####GLOBAL DISTANCES REF####



#we will now loop over each chromosome and use the bp position of each SNP to calculate the cM of each SNP
chroms = unique(snps.chroms$chromosome) #grab chrom names to loop over
chroms

results.mat = matrix(nrow = 1, ncol = 4) #create matrix to store genetic map results
colnames(results.mat) = c("locus", "chromosome", "position", "position_cM")


for (j in chroms){

  #subset to target chrom
  snps.chroms.uniq = subset(snps.chroms, chromosome == j)

  
  #calculate genetic distance from physical distance
  snps.chroms.uniq$position_cM = snps.chroms.uniq$position/770000

  
  #add results to matrix
  results.mat = rbind(results.mat, snps.chroms.uniq)
  
  
}


#format genetic map results
results.df = as.data.frame(results.mat[-1,])
head(results.df)
tail(results.df)
dim(results.df)

results.final = results.df[,c("locus", "chromosome", "position_cM")]
colnames(results.final) = c("locus", "chromosome", "position")

results.final$position = round(results.final$position, 2)
head(results.final)


#export genetic map results
write.table(results.final, "/Users/erincollins/Google Drive/My Drive/Erin's Projects/chipps_gone/snp_sites_prep2.txt", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t")


#create boxplot
head(results.final)

pdf("/Users/erincollins/Google Drive/My Drive/Erin's Projects/chipps_gone/genetic_map_distances.pdf", width = 12, height = 8)
ggplot(results.final, aes(x = chromosome, y = position)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#ff6666", color = "black") +
  scale_y_continuous("Distance (cM)", limits = c(0,120), breaks = seq(0,120,20)) +
  scale_x_discrete("Chromosome") +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 14), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 14)) +
  ggtitle("Genetic Distance (cM) - Global genetic distance")
dev.off()



```
